sources.entry: Artify - A macOS application for bringing dedicatedly 18th century Arts to everyone

summary.one_liner: Artify is a macOS app that generates wallpapers from hand-picked 18th-century paintings, sized to your screen, and fetches a new featured artwork each day.
summary.what_it_does: The app is a native macOS application written in Swift that uses RxSwift and MVVM. According to the README, it offers a hand-picked collection of 18th-century art and generates wallpapers sized to the current screen. It automatically fetches a featured artwork every day. The README describes a wallpaper pipeline that places the artwork in the middle of a scaled background, adds a shadow, applies a Gaussian blur, and caches the result locally. The README says the artworks come from WikiArt and that the app depends on a separate Golang backend called Artify Core. The on-demand choice of art style or artist is marked "Coming soon."
use_cases: Set an 18th-century painting as a daily desktop wallpaper
Generate screen-sized wallpapers from classic artworks
Browse famous paintings with artist and history details
Study or develop a macOS RxSwift MVVM app
how_to_run: Start the Artify Core backend (see the README's linked instructions)
notable: Wallpapers are generated per screen size using a described multi-step image pipeline with Gaussian blur
Daily automatic fetch of a featured artwork
Artworks are hand-picked from WikiArt, per the README
Backend is a separate Golang project called Artify Core
caveats: Requires the separate Artify Core backend to be running for development
Art style and artist selection is marked 'Coming soon'
